courses.title: Jewish life in exile and the wider world
courses.description: Six sessions in historical context, communal institutions, memory, translation, and responsible comparison.

sessions.title: Locate Jeremiah's audience
sessions.translation: Seek the welfare of the city.
choices: Who is addressed, in what setting, and for what purpose?
Which current position does it automatically settle?
How many letters are in the verse?
sessions.explanation: Historical reading begins with speaker, audience, setting, and purpose.

sessions.title: Read exile as a setting
sessions.translation: To which I have exiled you.
choices: It shapes the community question the verse addresses.
It makes the verse only a date.
sessions.explanation: Context is evidence for reading, not a replacement for the source.

sessions.title: Compare rabbinic worlds
sessions.prompt: What can this comparison help explain?
choices: How communities, language, and institutions shape questions.
sessions.explanation: Texts are studied by communities in particular places.

sessions.title: Name an institution
sessions.prompt: What does this cluster invite a learner to study?
choices: How learning, law, and belonging take social form.
sessions.explanation: Institutions sustain and reshape learning across time.

sessions.title: Treat memory as evidence
choices: A source can be evidence about an event and about how it was remembered.
Every source is a neutral camera.
sessions.explanation: Sources are both windows and voices.

sessions.title: Compare without flattening
sessions.prompt: What makes a wider-world comparison responsible?
choices: Name a shared question and preserve each source's context and difference.
sessions.explanation: Comparison is disciplined close reading across distinct worlds.

production.translation: Seek the welfare of the city.
production.prompt: This instruction anchored the course. Type its English meaning from memory, in a few words.
acceptable: seek the welfare of the city
seek the peace of the city
and seek the welfare of the city
and seek the peace of the city
seek the wellbeing of the city
